understand_h: Why a tooth may need to come out
understand:
Your dentist will always look at ways to keep a tooth first. Removal may be recommended when a tooth is too badly decayed or broken to repair, affected by advanced gum disease, causing repeated infection, or crowding other teeth.

Before an extraction your dentist will examine the tooth, usually take an X-ray, review your medical history and medicines, and explain what to expect and how the gap could be replaced if needed.

benefits: Removes a source of pain or infection
Can be the most predictable option for a tooth that can’t be saved
consider: A gap can affect chewing and allow teeth to drift
Healing takes time, and some people have swelling or discomfort
Let us know about blood thinners and other medicines beforehand
alternatives: Root canal therapy where the tooth can be saved
Replacing the tooth with an implant, bridge or denture

care: Bite firmly on the gauze as instructed. Rest, and avoid hot drinks until the numbness wears off.
Avoid rinsing hard, spitting forcefully, using straws and smoking, which can disturb the blood clot.
Choose soft foods and chew on the other side for a few days.
Brush your other teeth as normal. Your dentist will tell you when and how to rinse the area.
